reviews.text: I had hopes for Antivirus PROTOCOL to become more interesting than the demo I played a couple months ago. The full release still feels like a demo. The skill tree is nearly a straight line requiring level completion to continue with no interesting choices to make. The gameplay loop has three stages. You start by hovering directly over enemies. Then you kite green enemies. Then you look for blue enemies along the edge. There's only one boss shared across every 15 levels, and there's no other real way to approach the game with its limited system. There are a couple levels that are huge walls due to bad scaling. All other games I've played like this allow you to go back to a previous level, but this Antivirus PROTOCOL locks you into the new level. So, you end up spending several minutes grinding a handful of enemies until you build enough currency to finally get back into the linear progression. Honestly, I just can't find any reason I would recommend this game to someone.

You're lookin at it, you know it's not all that original but it's still got *the look*. it don't got the sauce though. typically you can grind in these games to make the number big enough to steam roll the content or just go from level to level with as much skill as you'd like and the latter seems to be the point with the whole "no replaying levels" gimmick. Unfortunately all it turns into is hitting a brick wall halfway through trying to numbers the boss' health to zero to be able to progress on the skill tree, the whole time collecting enough resources to max out all the new upgrades after finally beating the boss...and then getting stuck on the next boss again. There's like ten games exactly like this one if you haven't played them that are way better. If you have played them all and are looking for the next one, it might not be this one.

2.5 hrs for 100% achievements - Most restrictive and linear skill tree I've ever seen in an incremental game It makes sense for new weapons or new mechanics to be gated behind bosses but every uninteresting vanilla upgrades are gated behind bosses every time - No interesting upgrades. Flat power, flat damage, flat damage, flat damage, flat damage, flat power, flat damage, flat damage - 2.5 hours for $5 is unacceptable especially more so when the 2.5 hours was dragged on by uninteresting stat checks and gated linear skill tree - Zero replay value. Next playthrough you're gonna take the same boring upgrades in the same order in the same linear skill tree This feels more like a social experiment or a prank than a game

Wide as a puddle, and deep as a... oh wait, its deep as a puddle too... Definitely a letdown from the reasonably promising demo. A little on the shorter end too, even for this genre, coming in at around 2 and a half hours. This isn't totally I will say upfront that the game isn't TERRIBLE or completely unenjoyable, just exceptionally mediocre as far as a game like this goes. It is probably a bottom 10 or even bottom 5 short incremental game. For this mediocrity the game is overpriced too, probably being more in line with 2 dollars instead of 5. The comparison between this game and Astro Prospector, both in the same bundle and pricerange, is a night and day difference. Astro Prospector blows it out of the water in just about every metric. Starting with the main flaw of this game, its uncreative and extremely linear skill tree. As others will rightfully point out, this is the most restrictive skill tree you will find in the genre, it is so linear that it often feels like it is a skill tree in name only. Progression in the skill tree is effectively gated behind a currency only dropped by bosses. These bosses are tough enough that you generally have to buy most, if not all of the basic stat upgrades in order to beat them. And this leads to the other half of the skill tree issue; its just basic upgrades. Every level of the skill tree comes with a damage upgrade and a life upgrade, usually a virus spawnrate upgrade too. As the levels go up the upgrade variety decreases as well. Attack speed was given out too early, and maxes out quickly, but what I think really exemplifies the lack of thought and care with the gameplay is how armor upgrades just completely disappear after the early game. The game almost never goes beyond the absolute basics. There are critrate and double resource drop upgrades that max out at 35%, a better game would have had them max out at 100% and worked that into the progression (no unique synergy with either critrate or resource collection either) . There are no lifesteal upgrades at all, bare minimum quality of life, even most of the upgrades that require the boss currency are very basic. The game also has very subpar ability progression. You unlock the minigun almost instantly, but it is effectively the only permanent weapon you unlock until the last few levels at the end of the game. For a strange reason the game keeps on trying to push temporary (5 seconds at best) powerups as your main form of damage progression beyond the basic stat increases. These powerups are not super reliable, and not as satisfying as a dedicated weapon unlock. In particular the game keeps trying to push the "Shock" powerup on you, which sucks as a powerup when you get it and will never get better. You would think that this would become a basic weapon later on, but it doesn't. The gameplay is also very basic with no redeeming qualities. The normal red viruses don't do any contact damage or have any unique features. Occasionally a chasing suicide virus will spawn, which is probably the highlight of gameplay. It is reasonably fun to get the hang of dodging it since it moves quite quickly. The green viruses on the other hand are just annoying. They have significantly more health than standard viruses and charge you VERY quickly at close range. The problem is that all your weapons are close range, so you are forced to get close. If they manage to hit you, not only do they deal damage but they also don't drop their special resource. This is particularly annoying early on when you first unlock them and don't know what they are capable of yet. The other enemies are no better. Boss is effectively just a big red virus, white virus is just a rare red virus, blue virus shoots basic and annoying screenwide lasers... The only area of the game it does a decent job in is with the music and visual design, both of which are more than adequate for the standards of short incrementals. The pixelated CRT artstyle is used so often for good reason, although it certainly isn't helping this game beat the "bland and uncreative" allegations. Overall, this is certainly a short incremental game of all time. If you just wanna relax for a couple hours and not have to think deeply about anything, it might fit the bill. Otherwise, definitely look elsewhere for your incremental fix. There are enough of them out there these days that it will take quite a while before you run out of games better than this one. This review has been a bit harsh on it when it is still just "mid" but the standards of the genre have long outpaced games of subpar quality like this.

Now I have a lot to say about this game. Firstly I just want to express my absolute LOVE for the aesthetics of it. It's such a simplistic design with a touch of *WOW* and it's not overcomplicated. From the design of the enemies to the UI and "skill tree", it all harmonises with each other and makes it incredibly easy on the eyes and enjoyable to use. Secondly, I have never been a casual gamer, I've always been competitive and played "hard" games like soulsborne games etc. but this is one of the first games that has ever kept me hooked until completion while simultaneously being a really chilled out and relaxing experience. The skill balancing is VERY well done, where the upgrades make sense and the attention needed is just enough to stop it from being too laid back but also not too intense that you start having an adrenaline spike. Overall, the gameplay and mechanics are amazing! Lastly, the music is almost contrasting to the nature of the game, and further accentuates the chill vibe that I think the devs intended. Although it is the same 4-5 song (rough estimate as I was so hooked on the gameplay itself), but it never felt too repetitive or boring. All I have to say is VERY well done to the devs and thank you for making a game that's given me an amazing experience. - n2g

Antivirus Protocol feels like a missed opportunity in an increasingly crowded genre. While the incremental shooter/upgrade loop has potential, this game lacks the creativity seen in many other recent titles that are doing it much better. The balancing is currently quite poor, making the runs feel incredibly repetitive very quickly. A major issue is the total lack of "build expression." Instead of making strategic choices to overcome bosses, you’re essentially forced to grind and pick up every single upgrade just to progress. This kills any sense of player agency and creativity, making the gameplay feel far too linear. To make matters worse, there is no pause button during a run—a glaring omission for a game in 2026. Given the superior alternatives available right now, it's hard to recommend this in its current state.

So I was happy when finishing the game and got 100% Achievement, so I can put this aside and don't have to play it again. For people who like it to get poked while gathering stuff, it could probably be more fun then it was for me.

Pretty solid indie game, highly satisfying as it should be. I didn't finish it yet, but I don't really have anything bad to say about it. I love the power-ups and the fact that you have to pick them up, I love the sense of progression, the game is just a little bit hard (which is great, cause they tend to be easy) and doesn't make you feel stuck or bored when you have to replay a level. I think if I had to pick something, I'd say the skill tree is too straight forward, I'd like to have more options, like choosing a path between the mines power-up or the multishot, or some progression between upgrades of the same type (shot speed, battery...) that are connected (to keep the balance, maybe you should make the player go back to the first nodes, but only with a lot more resources, or make it appear only after some level). The way they're placed, they don't look like they're related to the power you get. Overall, I'm very happy with my purchase and I think it has some rizz to call its own. :)
